sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A deciduous, twining climber native from the Russian Far East through Korea and Japan to China. Its heart-shaped leaves can reach about 15 cm; small fragrant flowers are followed by greenish-orange berries up to about 2 cm. Some mature male plants develop pink-and-white leaf variegation. In cultivation it commonly climbs to around 4.5–6 m.

sections.title: Food and comparison
sections.text: The small fruits are eaten in Russia, and young leaves are used as a pot herb in East Asia. It is related to kiwifruit (Actinidia deliciosa), but has much smaller fruit and is also grown for its foliage.
